newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: 40 pct Portugal non-bank state firms profitable 95.
newsitem.headline: 40 pct Portugal non-bank state firms profitable 95.

text.p: About 40 percent of Portugal's non-bank public companies posted net profits in 1995, a report by a department of the Finance Ministry said.

"Among 42 non-financial public companies, 17 (that is, about 40 percent) presented net profits in 1995, whereas in the previous year, among the same number of companies, just 15 companies (some 36 percent) posted profits," said a study by the Office for the Analysis of Financing of the State and Public Companies (GAFEEP).
It said the total profits of the 17 non-bank public companies stood at 155.4 billion escudos in 1995, which was 59.8 billion more than the total profit achieved by the 15 companies in 1994.

More than 96 percent of the 1995 profits were obtained by just seven companies: EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, Portugal Telecom, cement producer Cimpor, motorway company Brisa, pulp producer Portucel Industrial, bus company RNIP and airport company ANA.
